text: In the beginning the Word already was; the Word was face to face with God, and the Word was God himself.
He was there with God from the very beginning.
Everything that exists came into being through him, and nothing that exists came into being without him.
Life itself was in him, and that life was the light of humankind.
The light shines on in the darkness, and the darkness has never put it out.
A man named John was sent from God as a messenger.
He came to bear witness about the light, so that everyone might come to believe through him.
He himself was not the light — he came only to testify about it.
The true light, the one who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
He was already in the world — the world he had made — yet the world did not recognize him.
He came to his own people, and his own people did not receive him.
But to everyone who did receive him, who trusted in his name, he gave the right to become children of God —
children born not by ordinary descent, nor by any human plan or desire, but born of God.
And the Word became flesh and took up residence among us; we saw his glory, glory belonging to the Father's one and only Son, full of grace and truth.
John testifies about him, crying out, 'This is the one I spoke of when I said, the one coming after me has passed ahead of me, because he existed before me.'
From the fullness of his grace we have all received one gift after another.
The law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God; but God's only Son, who is closest to the Father's own heart, has revealed him.
Now this was John's testimony when the Jerusalem leaders sent priests and Levites to ask him, 'Who are you?'
He did not evade the question but stated plainly, 'I am not the Christ.'
They asked, 'Then who are you — are you Elijah?' He said, 'I am not.' 'Are you the Prophet?' 'No,' he answered.
So they said, 'Then who are you? We need an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?'
He replied, 'I am a voice crying out in the wilderness: make the Lord's way straight — just as the prophet Isaiah said.'
Now the men had been sent by the Pharisees,
and they questioned him further, 'Why then are you baptizing, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?'
John answered them, 'I baptize with water. But among you stands someone you do not recognize —
the one coming after me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie.'
All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, 'Look — the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!'
'This is the one I meant when I said, after me comes a man who has passed ahead of me, because he existed before me.'
'I myself did not know him, but I came baptizing with water for this very reason — so that he might be revealed to Israel.'
Then John testified, 'I watched the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove, and it stayed on him.'
'I would not have known him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water told me, the man on whom you see the Spirit come down and remain — he is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'
'I have seen this myself, and I testify that this is the Son of God.'
The next day John was standing there again with two of his own followers.
When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, 'Look — the Lamb of God!'
The two followers heard him say this and went off after Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following and asked, 'What are you looking for?' They said, 'Rabbi — where are you staying?'
'Come and see,' he told them. So they went and saw where he was staying and spent the rest of that day with him — it was about the tenth hour.
One of the two who had heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.
The first thing Andrew did was find his own brother Simon and tell him, 'We have found the Messiah!' (which means Christ).
He brought Simon to Jesus. Looking at him, Jesus said, 'You are Simon, son of John — you will be called Cephas' (which is translated Peter, meaning 'rock').
The next day Jesus decided to head for Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, 'Follow me.'
Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and told him, 'We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, the one the Prophets wrote about too — Jesus of Nazareth, Joseph's son.'
'Nazareth!' said Nathanael. 'Can anything good come from there?' 'Come and see for yourself,' Philip replied.
As Nathanael approached, Jesus said of him, 'Here is a true Israelite — nothing false in him.'
Nathanael asked, 'How do you know me?' Jesus answered, 'Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.'
Nathanael exclaimed, 'Rabbi, you are the Son of God — you are the King of Israel!'
Jesus replied, 'You believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see far greater things than that.'
'Truly I tell you,' he went on, 'you will all see heaven opened and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man.'
